text: A guest wants to work on a laptop while sitting on a bed. Which bedrooms let them do both, based on the objects present? Watch for a bedroom that has one but not the other.

key_facts.fact: Bedroom [8] qualifies (it has both a Bed and a Laptop)
Bedroom [10] qualifies (it has both a Bed and a Laptop)
Bedroom [6] does not qualify because it has a Laptop but no Bed

text: Counting chairs, armchairs, and sofas as seats, which single room provides the most seating, and how many seats is that?

key_facts.fact: Kitchen [2] provides the most seating
Kitchen [2] has 3 seats: 2 Chairs and 1 ArmChair
No other room exceeds this (LivingRoom [3] and LivingRoom [5] have only one Sofa each)

text: Starting in Kitchen [2] and moving only through connected doorways, can you reach any bedroom? Explain using the room connections.

key_facts.fact: No bedroom is reachable from Kitchen [2] through doorways
Kitchen [2] connects only to LivingRoom [3], which connects only back to Kitchen [2], forming a closed pair
The bedrooms belong to a separate connected component centered on Bedroom [6]

text: If the doors of exactly one room were sealed, which room's removal would break the connected bedroom-and-bathroom area into separate disconnected groups? Explain why.

key_facts.fact: Sealing Bedroom [6] would disconnect the area
Bedroom [6] is the hub linking Bedroom [8] (with Bathroom [9]), Bedroom [10] (with Bathroom [11]), LivingRoom [4], and Bathroom [7]
Without Bedroom [6] these become isolated groups

text: How many doorways must you pass through to get from Bathroom [9] to Bathroom [11], and through which rooms?

key_facts.fact: You must pass through 4 doorways
The route is Bathroom [9] -> Bedroom [8] -> Bedroom [6] -> Bedroom [10] -> Bathroom [11]

text: Bathroom [7] and Bathroom [9] are physically very close to each other. Can you walk straight from one to the other through a single doorway? If not, give the shortest doorway route.

key_facts.fact: No, there is no direct doorway between Bathroom [7] and Bathroom [9]
The shortest doorway route is Bathroom [7] -> Bedroom [6] -> Bedroom [8] -> Bathroom [9], i.e. 3 doorways
Physical closeness does not imply a direct connection

text: Among the three bathrooms, which one is the most isolated, meaning its nearest fellow bathroom is farther away than for the other two? Support it with distances.

key_facts.fact: Bathroom [11] is the most isolated bathroom
Bathroom [11]'s nearest other bathroom is Bathroom [7] at about 6.5 m
Bathroom [7] and Bathroom [9] are only about 3.2 m apart, much closer

text: What is Kitchen [2]'s nearest neighboring room, and based on the distances involved, is the kitchen better described as central or peripheral within the home?

key_facts.fact: Kitchen [2]'s nearest room is LivingRoom [3], about 5.1 m away
The kitchen is peripheral: even its nearest room is farther than most rooms' nearest neighbours, which are around 2-3.5 m

text: Match each bedroom to its nearest bathroom by distance, and state whether those matches also correspond to direct doorway connections.

key_facts.fact: Bedroom [6]'s nearest bathroom is Bathroom [7] (about 2.9 m)
Bedroom [8]'s nearest bathroom is Bathroom [9] (about 3.5 m)
Bedroom [10]'s nearest bathroom is Bathroom [11] (about 3.4 m)
Each nearest-bathroom match also corresponds to a direct doorway connection

text: You are standing in Bedroom [6], facing toward Bathroom [7]. Relative to you, is Bedroom [8] on your left, on your right, ahead, or behind? Explain.

key_facts.fact: Bedroom [8] is on your left
From Bedroom [6], Bathroom [7] is to the north-east and Bedroom [8] is to the north-west, so when you face Bathroom [7], Bedroom [8] falls to your left

text: Travelling from Bathroom [7] to Bedroom [6] and then on to Bedroom [10], what compass heading do you take on each of the two legs?

key_facts.fact: From Bathroom [7] to Bedroom [6] you head south-west
From Bedroom [6] to Bedroom [10] you head east

text: Give turn-by-turn directions from Bathroom [9] to Bathroom [11]: list the rooms in order and the compass heading for each leg.

key_facts.fact: The room sequence is Bathroom [9] -> Bedroom [8] -> Bedroom [6] -> Bedroom [10] -> Bathroom [11]
The leg headings are south-west, then south-east, then east, then south

text: A delivery robot starts in LivingRoom [5] and must bring an item to Kitchen [2]. Can it get there through doorways? If not, explain what stops it.

key_facts.fact: No, the robot cannot reach Kitchen [2]
LivingRoom [5] has no doorway connections at all (it is isolated), so the robot cannot even leave the room
Even otherwise, the Kitchen belongs to a separate connected component

text: Counting each object type only once, which room contains the greatest variety of distinct object types? Roughly how many distinct types is that?

key_facts.fact: Kitchen [2] contains the greatest variety of distinct object types
It has roughly 25 distinct object types, clearly more than any other room

text: Which object type appears in the largest number of different rooms, and in how many of the 10 rooms does it appear?

key_facts.fact: Painting appears in the most rooms
It appears in 9 of the 10 rooms
The only room without a Painting is Bedroom [10]

text: Which object types are present in all three bedrooms (Bedroom [6], Bedroom [8], and Bedroom [10])?

key_facts.fact: CellPhone is in all three bedrooms
Laptop is in all three bedrooms
Dresser is in all three bedrooms
CellPhone, Laptop, and Dresser are the only object types common to all three bedrooms

text: Treat every room that contains a Toilet as a restroom. How many restrooms are there, and which rooms are they?

key_facts.fact: There are 3 restrooms
They are Bathroom [7], Bathroom [9], and Bathroom [11]
No room outside these three contains a Toilet

text: For a movie night you want a single room that has both a Sofa and a Television. Does any room qualify? If not, list which rooms have each.

key_facts.fact: No single room has both a Sofa and a Television
Sofas are in LivingRoom [3] and LivingRoom [5]
Televisions are in Kitchen [2] and Bedroom [6]

text: One of the three bedrooms is set up more like a home office than a place to sleep. Based only on the objects in each, which bedroom is it, and what makes it stand out?

key_facts.fact: Bedroom [6] is the one set up like a home office
Unlike Bedroom [8] and Bedroom [10], Bedroom [6] has no Bed
It instead holds work and media items such as a Laptop, DeskLamp, and Television
